svg.text: Figure 5 · Peak-Hour Interval Width as a Joint Function of Design Dials
Width (kW) at Summer typical-day peak hour, swept over participation-interval width and peak-period tariff η
Each cell reports the proposed-method 24-h interval width at the Summer-typical-day peak hour, in kW, as both design dials are swept independently. The
response is approximately linear in either dial within the studied window, and a designer can navigate the surface by trading participation-bound tightness
against day-ahead tariff-band tightness. The dashed square marks the operating point used in Figs. 2-4.
